channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Nature: Lead carboxylates passivation for meter-scale perovskite solar modules
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10994-7 Lead carboxylates passivation for meter-scale perovskite solar modules

item.title: Nature: Pre-clinical data interpretation requires clinical context
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10774-3 Pre-clinical data interpretation requires clinical context

item.title: Nature: The probiotic bacteria engineered to treat diabetes
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02521-5 Genetically modified bacteria lower high blood-sugar in animal trials — plus, how to watch a solar eclipse safely.

item.title: Nature: Dataset artefacts can partially drive the measured decline in disruption
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10787-y Dataset artefacts can partially drive the measured decline in disruption

item.title: Nature: Agentic profiles for effective AI governance
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10805-z A framework comprising four dimensions—autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity and generality—is proposed for characterizing AI agents, supporting the construction of agentic profiles for the effective governance of different AI agents.

item.title: Nature: Glucose-responsive probiotics for glycaemic modulation in mice and monkeys
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10909-6 Engineered probiotics equipped with a synthetic glucose-responsive circuit transiently colonize the gut and secrete therapeutic factors when glucose levels increase, enabling safe, oral, sense-and-respond control of diabetes in mouse and primate models.

item.title: Nature: Temporal uncoupling of radial glia lineage progression in cortical organoids
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10916-7 RGP lineage tracing in stem-cell-derived organoids shows highly plastic proliferation and reduced clonal neuronal diversity, indicating that missing non-cell-autonomous niche cues are essential for faithful temporal control of cortical lineage progression.

item.title: Nature: Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10888-8 Tracing cascading continental-scale medieval megafloods across Europe indicates that current flood management is unprepared for such sequences, highlighting the urgent need for proactive flood risk management strategies that account for unusual series of extreme flood events.

item.title: Nature: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10886-w CDK4/6 inhibition redirects Rb chromatin occupancy to activate oestrogen-responsive genes, counteracting its own ability to maintain therapeutic cell-cycle arrest.

item.title: Nature: Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10907-8 Expression of Meis2 in hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in an adult mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders rescues experience-dependent plasticity, improves memory and network function and suppresses seizures.

item.title: Nature: A gas-enshrouded and gas-reddened black hole at cosmic dawn
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10846-4 Observations of an unusual cosmic-dawn source illuminate how early supermassive black holes may have grown rapidly in a gas-enshrouded state; such enshrouded black holes may lie at the heart of the 'little red dots'.

item.title: Nature: Towards an equitable future of global photovoltaic waste recycling
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10905-w Global photovoltaic waste will reach 297–402 million tonnes by 2060, and regionally adapted recycling strategies and international cooperation will be needed to provide equitable and scalable PV waste circularity.

item.title: Nature: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10889-7 A new chemistry-based super-resolution imaging framework is described, enabling 3D, laser-free, highly sensitive and ultralong-term imaging of live cells which overcomes the limitations in spatiotemporal resolution associated with reaction-based imaging methods.

item.title: Nature: Degree-of-polarization modulation for high-dimensional optical computing
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10891-z By engineering the statistics of light at the micrometre scale using phase-only spatial light modulators, both the state and degree of polarization become spatially programmable, enabling direct encoding of information in a high-dimensional space.

item.title: Nature: Neural basis of compositional control
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10896-8 Behaviour of human participants in a prey-pursuit task reflects dynamic blending of goal-specific control policies, with hippocampus estimating latent states, anterior cingulate cortex orchestrating policy switches and orbitofrontal cortex supplying value-based contextualization rather than driving continuous policy updating.

item.title: Nature: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10903-y Cryo-electron microscopy structures show how IS621 bridge recombinase mediates DNA excision, explaining its natural preference for insertion and informing the design of programmable bridge-editing technologies.

item.title: Nature: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10870-4 Substantial intraspecific variation, together with species turnover, drives coordinated shifts in drought resistance such as increased embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins in drier forests.

item.title: Nature: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10724-z Shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope, provide evidence for the recycling of fragmented stellar ejecta into the surrounding gas.

item.title: Nature: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10922-9 The maternal gut microbiome is a predictor of infant eczema.

item.title: Nature: Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10878-w Deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1 reveals an extragalactic globular cluster stream, with analysis and modelling probing the rich dark matter content of the host galaxy.

item.title: Nature: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10880-2 An analysis of the relationships between aboveground biomass and various climatic factors in three major regions of tropical forest shows that understanding the complex interactions between climate, topography and soils is crucial to predict how climate change will affect carbon storage capacity.

item.title: Nature: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO 2 plane
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10857-1 A high-quality, pristine monolayer cuprate superconductor with a single CuO2 plane is fabricated and used to identify two quantum critical phenomena emerging between the Mott insulating phase and the superconducting phase.

item.title: Nature: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10906-9 An in vivo model that is able to recover human T cells from solid tumours can identify targets to help improve CAR T cell antitumour activity.

item.title: Nature: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10925-6 Potential predictive biomarkers of perioperative nivolumab therapy benefit in non-small cell lung cancer are identified from evaluable participants in the CheckMate 77T trial.

item.title: Nature: Intraspecific variation in tropical trees can drive resistance to drought
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02292-z Different tropical tree species can vary in their ability to withstand drought — and so too, it seems, can distinct populations of the same tree species.

item.title: Nature: ‘Little red dot’ gets its colour from gas — not dust
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02290-1 Dust can tint the cosmos red, but a compact astronomical object is coloured by turbulent gas around a black hole.

item.title: Nature: No single rule explains how climate affects carbon storage in tropical forests
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02291-0 Ecologists have long wondered why some tropical forests store more carbon than others. A global satellite survey offers an explanation.

item.title: Nature: Trump wants MMR vaccine split up: the science behind why it’s a bad idea
item.description: Nature, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02515-3 Numerous studies have shown that separating childhood jabs will delay protection and increase costs for families.

item.title: Cell: Pangenome-guided breeding restores high-altitude adaptation and improves yield in Tartary buckwheat
item.description: A Tartary buckwheat pangenome is constructed, allowing identification of the wild-specific gene FtRNH conferring high-altitude adaptation, as well as FtPLATZ structural variants controlling seed size. By combining these superior alleles, buckwheat lines are developed with enhanced high-altitude adaptability and improved field yields.

item.title: Cell: Trans-regulatory gene mapping prioritizes disease drivers in asthma
item.description: DANDELION is a causal mediation-inspired framework enabling the identification of disease-driving genes missed by existing approaches. Applied to asthma, DANDELION prioritizes two protein palmitoylation enzymes, revealing a therapeutically tractable pathway that is an important and previously unexplored mechanism underlying asthma pathogenesis.

item.title: Cell: Hierarchical and context-dependent encoding of actions in human posterior parietal and motor cortex
item.description: Interpreting others' actions is widely thought to rely on mirroring, yet direct neurophysiological evidence in humans remains scarce. Using single-neuron recordings from motor and posterior parietal cortex in tetraplegic participants, this study reveals hierarchical, context-dependent action coding: motor cortex encodes intentions, while posterior parietal cortex links observed actions to goals.

item.title: Cell: Convergent evolution of metabolic regulation governs redox adaptation in Toxoplasma
item.description: A protein called TgPRO enables the metabolic adaptation and survival of apicomplexan parasites such as Toxoplasma under oxidative and nutrient stress.

item.title: Cell: The sex and reproductive plasticity of intestinal muscles instruct gut size
item.description: Adult intestinal size plasticity is driven not only by epithelial stem cells but also by remodeling of the surrounding visceral musculature. Sex- and reproduction-dependent muscle remodeling controls gut size and transit, revealing the intestinal muscle as an active regulator of adult organ adaptation.

item.title: Nature: Phosphine-mediated azine C–H couplings with water and ammonia
item.description: Nature, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10991-w Phosphine-mediated azine C–H couplings with water and ammonia

item.title: Nature: The case for responsible scientific activism
item.description: Nature, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02464-x The case for responsible scientific activism

item.title: Nature: AI tools speed up analysis, but scientific truths must be grounded in reality
item.description: Nature, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02490-9 AI tools speed up analysis, but scientific truths must be grounded in reality

item.title: Nature: HIV vaccines guide rare immune cells to make broadly neutralizing antibodies
item.description: Nature, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02374-y Three studies in non-human primates show that strategically designed vaccines could prime a population of B cells to produce effective antibodies against HIV.

item.title: Nature: Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres
item.description: Nature, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02451-2 Publicly available AI models and local infrastructure can reduce AI’s environmental footprint while giving researchers greater control over the tools they use.

item.title: Cell: The structural basis for LRRK2’s activation and autoinhibition
item.description: Elevated kinase activity in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is linked to Parkinson’s disease; this study shows that its ROC GTPase acts as a nucleotide-dependent molecular switch that regulates activation and autoinhibition and reveals how some but not all PD mutations disrupt this regulatory switch.

item.title: Nature: Learning millisecond protein dynamics from what is missing in NMR spectra
item.description: Nature, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10989-4 Learning millisecond protein dynamics from what is missing in NMR spectra

item.title: Nature: Why environmental treaties must also address mental health
item.description: Nature, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02450-3 Global conventions have mainly overlooked the psychological and social impacts of climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution. Here’s how to change that.

item.title: Nature: Briefing Chat: Is DNA repair the secret to a long life? Whales and mole rats offer tantalizing hints
item.description: Nature, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02488-3 Nature staff discuss how animal studies are starting to uncover how DNA repair could prolong life, and how COVID-19 can reawaken dormant viruses.

item.title: Cell: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer
item.description: Spatial multi-omics reveals macrophage states that constrain adaptive immunity in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer.

item.title: Cell: Targeting peripheral 5-HT2AR enhances antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer
item.description: By selectively targeting peripheral 5-HT2AR without inducing psychedelic effects, a non-brain-penetrant agonist boosts antitumor CD8+ T cell immunity and improves immunotherapy responses in preclinical models of colorectal cancer.

item.title: Cell: Metabolic atlas of early human cortex reveals glycolytic remodeling and pentose phosphate pathway control of cell fate transitions
item.description: The developing human cortex is composed of diverse cell types, but how nutrient metabolism shapes their fate has remained unclear. This study maps the metabolic landscape of the developing human cortex and identifies glycolysis and pentose phosphate pathway activity as key regulators of radial glia fate, controlling the generation of outer radial glia and inhibitory neurons.

item.title: Cell: Distinct cellular phenotypes of language and executive decline in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: Beyond its motor dimension, ALS can also involve cognitive impairment, with affected domains varying across individuals. Rather than a single common disease process, this heterogeneity reflects regionally and cellularly distinct alterations in the prefrontal cortex that are only partially predicted by TDP-43 neuropathology.

item.title: Cell: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
item.description: ULTRA compresses 3D histology from days or hours to within 30 minutes by leveraging the chemical specificity of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy through the synergistic development of rapid tissue clearing and unsupervised AI. The platform enables intraoperative visualization of glioma architecture and depth-dependent tumor infiltration margins.

item.title: Cell: Milk osteopontin alters the infant microbiome to drive DC hematopoiesis and disease tolerance
item.description: Milk-derived osteopontin confers protection from viral or bacterial severe lower respiratory illness by altering the neonatal gut microbiome.

item.title: Cell: Co-option of retrotransposons promotes antibody diversification
item.description: A longstanding mystery in antibody diversification is how AID specifically targets immunoglobulin V genes. Ancient LINE-1 retrotransposons embedded within the immunoglobulin locus provide a recruitment platform for the HUSH complex and AID to drive somatic hypermutation.

item.title: Cell: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles
item.description: An integrative cell and spatial atlas defines the organizing logic of the adult human cerebrovasculature, providing a framework for studying how vascular cell states support brain function and shape neurological disease vulnerability.

item.title: Cell: Dietary arginine drives codon-dependent MHC class I translation and improves immunity in colon tumorigenesis and respiratory viral infection
item.description: Arginine availability regulates arginyl tRNA levels and codon-dependent translation of MHC class I, tuning antigen presentation and shaping anti-viral and anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: Basement membrane turnover controls cell shape
item.description: Basement membranes are scaffolds of proteins, like collagen, that give organs shape. During development, basement membranes must adapt to the growing organ. We infer how fast the basement membrane adapts by measuring collagen turnover. We find that perlecan, another basement membrane protein, regulates collagen turnover to control organ shape.

item.title: Cell: CRISPR screens identify targets to rescue age-related T cell dysfunction in cancer
item.description: Dusp5 and Zfp219 serve as critical regulators of age-related T cell dysfunction, with the loss of either driving T cells into an effector-like state that improves tumor control through distinct mechanisms within the aged tumor microenvironment.

item.title: Cell: Gasdermin E couples viral pyroptosis to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation
item.description: Wetland virus activates dual apoptotic cascades to trigger GSDME-dependent hepatocyte pyroptosis, which rewires cellular lipid metabolism and ultimately causes severe hepatic steatosis. Therapeutic targeting of this pyroptosis-metabolism axis alleviates lethal wetland virus infection in mice.

item.title: Cell: Advancing cancer detection and treatment using longitudinal routine clinical data
item.description: Liu et al. develop Oncoformer, a multimodal transformer that reads routine laboratory tests and chest X-rays already collected in everyday care. Across more than 3.6 million individuals, it detects cancer, infers tumor stage, and stratifies treatment response and recurrence risk, pointing toward risk-adapted cancer care built on data already in hand.

item.title: Cell: Dynamic dimer-of-dimers architecture defines Mg2+ transport in human CNNM4
item.description: Cryoelectron microscopy structures of human CNNM4 in distinct conformational states reveal how an unexpected dimer-of-asymmetric-dimers architecture mediates Mg2+/Na+ exchange and identify an intracellular acidic patch that may function in cellular magnesium sensing.

item.title: Cell: An Oryza orphan gene confers trans-species drought tolerance
item.description: ROAD1 is an Oryza-specific orphan gene that co-opts conserved ABA signaling to enhance drought tolerance without obvious growth defects or yield penalty under normal conditions. Elite rice lines carrying its functional allele exhibited higher grain yield than controls under drought, and its heterologous expression enhanced drought tolerance across diverse angiosperms.

item.title: Cell: Trichoderma swollenin activates AtABCB5-dependent auxin efflux to promote plant development
item.description: The beneficial fungus Trichoderma acts through the secreted swollenin ThSWO, which crosses the plant cell wall and engages AtABCB5, an auxin efflux carrier, at the host cell surface. This effector-transporter module tunes auxin-associated cellular responses, revealing how beneficial fungi co-opt host hormone transport to promote root development.

item.title: Cell: Condensates of the chromatin regulator ANKRD11 restrict hypertranscribed genes to safeguard development
item.description: ANKRD11 restricts hypertranscribed genes by forming biomolecular condensates that spatially sequester elongation factors, with disruption of this condensate-mediated control leading to aberrant organogenesis and underlying the pathogenesis of developmental disorders like KBG syndrome.

item.title: Cell: The intrinsic cardiac nervous system is essential for cardiac function and survival
item.description: Two genetically distinct neuronal subtypes in the intrinsic cardiac nervous system are differentially required for baseline cardiac function and stress resilience to maintain cardiac stability and survival.

item.title: Cell: A domestication-selected enhancer coordinates source-sink balance to improve harvest index and yield in maize
item.description: A teosinte-derived enhancer boosts the harvest index and grain yield in maize by optimizing source-to-sink carbon and nitrogen allocation, revealing a physiological pathway to yield during maize domestication.

item.title: Cell: Localized PD-1 CAR T therapy reprograms neuroinflammation
item.description: PD-1+ T follicular helper-like cells drive B cell-associated pathology in multiple sclerosis. Programmable PD-1-targeting CAR T cells selectively eliminate these pathogenic CD4 T cells while delivering IL-10 at sites of inflammation, thereby suppressing neuroinflammation across preclinical models.

item.title: Cell: CSF clearance through arachnoid fenestrations to olfactory meningeal lymphatics
item.description: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) crosses arachnoid fenestrations near the olfactory bulbs to reach dural lymphatics that traverse the cribriform plate, connect to nasal lymphatics, and drain to cervical lymph nodes. Aging impairs this pathway, but intranasal VEGF-C restores the lymphatics and the CSF outflow.

item.title: Cell: A bivalent molecular glue linking lysine acetyltransferases to oncogene-induced cell death
item.description: Chemically induced proximity of lysine acetyltransferases (KATs) with BCL6 reprograms epigenetic signaling to eliminate lymphoma tumors. Structural and mechanistic studies demonstrate that fortuitous protein-protein contacts convert proximity induction into targeted changes in chromatin, revealing a key mechanism by which small molecules can co-opt oncogenic transcriptional regulators to elicit malignant cell death.

item.title: Cell: Viral protease-initiated lytic cell death as a universal antiviral mRNA therapy
item.description: VIDA mRNA enables universal broad-spectrum antiviral therapy by triggering viral protease-initiated lytic cell death to eliminate infected cells and activate protective immunity.

item.title: Cell: Robust regulatory interplay of enhancers, facilitators, and promoters in a native chromatin context
item.description: Using an in situ genome-rewriting platform, Zhou et al. demonstrate that precise transcriptional regulation of the NMU promoter is governed by a 3D regulatory hub comprising a core retroviral LTR enhancer, a decoy LTR promoter, and activity-boosting “facilitator” elements.

item.title: Cell: Skin-innervating glutamatergic neurons modulate aging
item.description: Within the skin, glutamatergic neurons expressing neurofilament heavy chain (Nefh) play a role in aging. Loss of Nefh during aging drives skin fibroblast senescence and collagen loss, whereas glutamate supplementation improves skin aging phenotypes.

item.title: Cell: Spatial proximity sequencing maps developmental dynamics in the germinal center
item.description: Sprox-seq enables spatial profiling of protein complexes, surface proteins, and mRNAs in intact tissues by combining proximity ligation with spatial transcriptomics. In human tonsils, Sprox-seq maps germinal center interaction networks, links CD21-CD35 complexes to proliferative programs, reveals interaction-based B cell state transitions, and directly captures B cell-follicular dendritic cell communication.

item.title: Cell: Boron-bridged GIPCs stabilize cell wall anchoring and PIN polar domains
item.description: Boron cross-links glycosylinositol phosphorylceramides (GIPCs) to physically tether the plasma membrane to the cell wall in plant cells, stabilizing PIN polar domains via direct lipid-protein interaction and enabling polar auxin transport.

item.title: Cell: Whole-transcriptome-scale isoform-resolved spatial imaging of single cells in tissues
item.description: RT&T-AMP-MERFISH enables whole-transcriptome-scale, isoform-resolved spatial imaging of single cells in intact tissues and reveals how gene programs and transcript isoform usage vary across cell types and anatomical regions in the brain.

item.title: Cell: A viral ORFeome library for systems-level genetic dissection of host-pathogen interactions
item.description: A scalable library of ∼13,000 barcoded viral open reading frames from >500 viral species enables functional genomic screens across the virome. Applying this platform identified viral regulators of cellular proliferation, antigen presentation, and interferon signaling. This platform enables systematic exploration of viral protein function.

item.title: Cell: Four-dimensional molecular mapping from a spatial snapshot reveals the dynamics of hair follicle organogenesis
item.description: A deep-tissue spatial transcriptomics method simultaneously captures hundreds of hair follicles spanning organogenesis in mouse skin. Ordering follicles by molecular age transforms this snapshot into a map of organogenesis in both space and time, revealing the choreography of organ assembly and how it goes awry in genetically hairless mice.

item.title: Cell: Co-option of lysosomal machinery shapes the evolution of the intracellular photosymbiosis supporting coral reefs
item.description: Corals harbor intracellular algal symbionts in specialized organelles that enable them to build diverse reef ecosystems. Corals and other cnidarians have repeatedly evolved this symbiosis through the co-option of lysosomal machinery to simultaneously support photosynthesis and extract photosynthetic products from the algae.

item.title: Cell: Recurrent patterns of TOP1-mediated neuronal genomic damage shared by major neurodegenerative disorders
item.description: Single-cell whole-genome sequencing reveals a shared pattern of excessive somatic mutations across C9ORF72 ALS, C9ORF72 FTD, and Alzheimer’s disease, dominated by 2-bp deletions. These mutations arise from aberrant topoisomerase 1 (TOP1)-mediated mutagenesis linked to oxidative DNA damage, identifying a unifying mechanism of neuronal genomic instability in neurodegeneration.

item.title: Cell: Systematic discovery of pathogen effector functions across human pathogens and pathways
item.description: The eORFeome, a large-scale collection of open reading frames encoding viral proteins and secreted bacterial and parasite effectors, enables functional genomics across diverse pathways and pathogens. Pooled lentiviral screens identify pathogen effectors that perturb NF-κB, p53, apoptosis, STING, and MHC-I display pathways in human cells.

item.title: Cell: Structural basis for host membrane binding and remodeling by invading malaria parasites
item.description: Isolation and high-resolution structure of the moving junction protein complex from invading malaria parasites reveals an intricate molecular machine that bridges the host-pathogen interface and informs the de novo design of a small protein binder that inhibits parasite entry into host cells.

item.title: Cell: Multiscale integration of tissue and chromatin context converts cell heterogeneity into stable intestinal patterning
item.description: During regeneration, tissues must translate transient cellular variability into stable spatial organization. Tissue architecture generates a density-dependent window of heterogeneity in the mechanosensor YAP1 that FOXA1 integrates with Delta-Notch signaling, thereby linking tissue-scale mechanics to bistable cell fate decisions and stable tissue patterning.

item.title: Cell: Excessive epithelial mechanosensation drives nociceptive innervation and chronic bladder pain via the PIEZO1-SLC7A11-glutamate axis
item.description: Chronic bladder infection rewires epithelial mechanotransduction through IL-6-dependent PIEZO1 activation, triggering glutamate-mediated nociceptive hyperinnervation and persistent bladder pain. These findings identify a neuroepithelial pathway linking epithelial stress to chronic visceral pain.

item.title: Cell: Geometric constraints on the architecture of mammalian cortical connectomes
item.description: The origins of the cortical connectome’s complex topology and region-specific topography remain unclear, motivating a search for underlying physical principles. A neural-field-theory model that prioritizes connections between regions that facilitate the excitation of the resonant geometric eigenmodes of the cortex and reproduces topological and topographical features of diffusion-MRI and tract-tracing connectomes across five mammalian species and multiple spatial scales, indicating a universal geometric basis for connectome architecture.

item.title: Cell: Reconstituting human primitive streak formation through extra-embryonic cell coordination
item.description: Tissue patterning events of early human embryo development, including an embryo-disc with primitive streak-like structures, are captured using an in vitro model where embryonic stem cells are cultured with extra-embryonic cell types.

item.title: Cell: Cuproptosis-immunity crosstalk informs strategy to overcome immunotherapy resistance
item.description: A reciprocal circuit links cuproptosis and antitumor immunity, in which CD8⁺ T cell-derived IFN-γ enhances tumor susceptibility to cuproptosis. Engagement of this axis with PD-L1 blockade amplifies tumor cell killing and overcomes immunotherapy resistance.

item.title: Cell: Expansion and CAR engineering of granulocyte-monocyte progenitors for cellular immunotherapy
item.description: This study establishes granulocyte-monocyte progenitors as a renewable upstream platform for engineered myeloid cell therapy and introduces a CAR-Fc strategy that couples direct tumor targeting to host antigen-presenting cell activation.

item.title: Cell: Chloroplast sunscreening by protein condensates confers high-light tolerance
item.description: The conserved MBS1 protein assembles into chloroplast-associated condensates to sense singlet oxygen and shield chloroplasts against excess light penetration.

item.title: Cell: The critical role of the endogenous immune compartment after CAR T cell therapy in recurrent GBM
item.description: Single intracerebroventricular CAR T cell dose in patients with recurrent glioblastoma induces dose-dependent endogenous immune remodeling. Cytotoxic NK cell expansion is associated with prolonged survival, whereas Treg expansion and baseline scavenger myeloid cells are associated with poor outcomes.

item.title: Cell: Complete biosynthesis of the anticancer cephalotaxinone and homoerythratine
item.description: Complete biosynthetic pathways for cephalotaxinone and homoerythratine were elucidated from the endangered plant Cephalotaxus fortunei. Thirteen key enzymes were identified, including two homologous cytochrome P450 enzymes that catalyze a rare divergent oxidation process governing alkaloid scaffold diversification. Full pathway reconstitution in Nicotiana benthamiana establishes a foundation for the sustainable production of the anticancer agent homoharringtonine.

item.title: Cell: Prion-based protein self-assembly tunes mutagenesis to enable rapid adaptation
item.description: Prion-based protein self-assembly enables reversible switching of genome-maintenance pathways during rapid adaptation and the emergence of drug resistance.
